newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India GDRs lifted by interest cut.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India GDRs lifted by interest cut.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts finished in positive territory on Wednesday, rising sharply in afternoon trading following a move by India's central bank to cut interest rates, traders said.
The Reserve Bank of India's cut of 100 basis points to 10 percent came after trading had closed in local markets, and lifted London trading of GDRs out of an early morning trough, traders said.
"Prices hardened substantially, then there was a bit of selling into strength but the market ended firmly," a broker said.
The rate cut is seen as helping financial institutions as well as companies with higher levels of gearing.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.86 points higher at 88.32, with the premium over the local market at 26.08 percent from 24.15 percent.
Bombay's benchmark index fell 25.77 points to 4,093.62.
The market on Thursday will be focused on Reliance, which is set to announced the details of a bonus share issue.
Consensus among traders is that the issue will be about three shares for every five shares owned, but a more generous bonus would not come as a surprise, sources said.
Reliance ended the day two cents down at $22.50/$23.25. State Bank of India shares were cheered by the rate cut, rising 67 cents to $25.50/$26.35.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index closed down 0.39 points, or 0.52 percent, at 75.70 points, a premium of 41.25 percent over the local market.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index finished 3.30 points higher at 130.57, representing a discount to the local market of 3.48 percent.
